notes: Census Bureau release PDF exactly as served (3 pages; the PDF is untagged, so headings and tables are judged from the rendered pages only). Ground truth was built from the rendered pages (each page read as an image; both tables and the tightly set page-3 lines re-checked at 200 dpi); pdftotext and pdfplumber were used only to locate text and to check characters, fonts and colours. The text layer of the tables, the table captions and notes, the footnotes and parts of page 3 has few or no space characters between words (pdftotext -raw gives e.g. 'EstimatedQuarterlyU.S.RetailSales' and 'preliminary estimate.Therefore,theestimateissubjectto'); the expected strings use the spaced wording a reader sees on the page, so this file measures whether a converter recovers word spacing. The masthead ('U.S. Census Bureau News / U.S. Department of Commerce, Washington, D.C. 20233') and the chart body (axis labels, legend) are images without a text layer and are not checked; the chart title and 'Percent of Total' are real text. Noise: there is no visible running header, footer or page label; the only invisible text-layer item is a single white 5-pt '.' under the Table 1 subtitle on page 2, too short to check, so noise is empty. Headings are the release title (Calibri Bold 14 pt; body text is 10 pt) and the three page-3 section headings 'Survey Description', 'Adjusted Estimates' and 'Reliability of Estimates' (bold, each on its own line, same 10.5 pt size as the body); the bold 'Data Inquiries' / 'Media Inquiries' labels and the bold release-date paragraph on page 1 are body text, and the chart and table titles are captions, so none of them is listed. Ordered anchors come from the release line, the page-1 paragraphs, the Table 1 subtitle, the Table 2 title, a page-3 heading and the last page-3 sentence; none comes from a footnote, a table legend or a table note, so where a converter places footnotes does not affect the order score. Tables: both are complete; header rows are given top level first; a spanning header is placed in the first column it covers and the columns it also covers are empty; 'Quarter' and the single-column header 'E-commerce as a Percent of Total' (and in Table 2 'Standard Error (SE) for E-commerce as a Percent of Total') span both header rows and are placed in the top row. Table 1 has 14 rows: the two header rows, the bold row-group label 'Adjusted' with the superscript marker of footnote 2 (written 'Adjusted²', which NFKC-normalizes to 'adjusted2', so 'Adjusted2' also matches but 'Adjusted' without the marker does not; the corpus writes footnote markers in cells the same way, e.g. 'New fee¹' in the Federal Register file), its 5 quarter rows, the label 'Not Adjusted' and its 5 quarter rows; the two label rows have text only in the Quarter column. '(p)' and '(r)' are printed directly after the year without a space. Negative values use the ASCII hyphen-minus, as in the text layer. Hyphenation: the only line-end hyphens are in the true compounds 'E-commerce' (Table 2 title, 'Total and E-' / 'commerce') and 'X-11' (page 3, 'with the X-' / '11 filter-based adjustments'); both keep their hyphen when joined, so absent is empty (absent lists only split forms of words that are printed unhyphenated) and no checked string crosses either break. AUDIT 2026-11-24: (1) ordered: 'Estimate is less than 0.05%' (the '(Z)' legend line under Table 2, footnote-type text) replaced by 'Sampling Variability for Quarterly U.S. Retail Sales Estimates' (the Table 2 title, at the same point in reading order), so the order test no longer depends on where table footnotes are placed. (2) tables: Table 1 made complete by adding the row-group label rows 'Adjusted²' and 'Not Adjusted' (the old 12-row cap no longer applies; the old note also miscounted 13 printed rows below the header, there are 12); name updated. (3) absent: removed 'E- commerce' and 'X- 11', split forms of true compounds, which the absent rule excludes. (4) stresses: the hyphenated-compound item now says it is not scored. (5) notes: invisible white '.' recorded, heading styling and anchor sources stated. All must_contain phrases (each at least 6 words, each occurring once in the document), ordered anchors, headings and every table cell were re-checked character by character against the rendered pages; no other change. sha256 re-computed on the corpus file: unchanged.
